text_note.zh: 原始资料的题目只剩一个“大”字，是残缺的，词牌应为《大酺》，题目一般作“春雨”。第九句原作“吹沾帘竹”，通行本（如《宋词三百首》）作“吹黏帘竹”，意思是蛛网被风吹得粘在竹帘上，这里从通行本。
text_note.en: The source title has only its first character left. The tune is Dapu (Grand Feast), and the title is usually "Spring Rain". In line 9 the source has zhān (to moisten); common editions such as Three Hundred Song Lyrics have nián (to stick), meaning the cobwebs are blown and stuck to the bamboo blind. The common text is used here.

readings.zh: 流潦：路上流淌的雨水。“潦”指雨后的积水，读 lǎo，不读 liáo（潦草）。
readings.en: liú lǎo: rainwater running over the road. Here the character means standing rainwater and is read lǎo, not liáo.

readings.zh: 哀曲：悲伤的曲子，“曲”是乐曲，读 qǔ。
readings.en: āi qǔ: a sad tune. Here the character means a piece of music and is read qǔ.

glosses.zh: 对宿烟收：对面一夜的烟雾刚刚散去。宿，隔夜的。
glosses.en: duì sù yān shōu: the mist that hung all night across the way has just cleared. Sù means "from the night before".

glosses.zh: 春禽：春天的鸟。
glosses.en: chūn qín: spring birds.

glosses.zh: 高屋：高高的屋顶。
glosses.en: gāo wū: the high roof.

glosses.zh: 青玉旆：青玉色的旗子，比喻墙头一竿竿新竹。
glosses.en: qīng yù pèi: green-jade banners, meaning the new bamboo stalks above the wall.

glosses.zh: 铅霜：新竹表面那层白粉，像铅粉和霜。
glosses.en: qiān shuāng: the white powder on new bamboo, like lead powder or frost.

glosses.zh: 嫩梢相触：嫩嫩的竹梢互相碰来碰去。
glosses.en: nèn shāo xiāng chù: the tender bamboo tips brush against each other.

glosses.zh: 润逼琴丝：潮气逼进了琴弦。
glosses.en: rùn bī qín sī: the damp presses into the qin strings.

glosses.zh: 枕障：枕边的小屏风。
glosses.en: zhěn zhàng: the little screen by the pillow.

glosses.zh: 虫网：蜘蛛网。
glosses.en: chóng wǎng: cobwebs.

glosses.zh: 帘竹：竹帘。
glosses.en: lián zhú: the bamboo blind.

glosses.zh: 邮亭：古代路边给送信的人和旅客歇脚的驿站。
glosses.en: yóu tíng: a roadside post station where messengers and travelers rested.

glosses.zh: 檐声：雨水从屋檐滴下的声音。
glosses.en: yán shēng: the sound of rain dripping from the eaves.

glosses.zh: 困眠初熟：困了，刚刚睡熟。
glosses.en: kùn mián chū shú: tired, just fallen sound asleep.

glosses.zh: 奈：无奈，可惜。
glosses.en: nài: alas.

glosses.zh: 顿惊：一下子惊醒。
glosses.en: dùn jīng: suddenly woken.

glosses.zh: 梦轻：梦很浅很淡。
glosses.en: mèng qīng: the dream was light and faint.

glosses.zh: 幽独：孤孤单单，冷冷清清。
glosses.en: yōu dú: lonely and alone.

glosses.zh: 行人：在外赶路的人，这里是词人自己。
glosses.en: xíng rén: a traveler on the road, here the poet himself.

glosses.zh: 妨车毂：妨碍车轮转动，车走不了。车毂是车轮中心的圆木。
glosses.en: fáng chē gǔ: getting in the way of the wheels so the cart cannot go. The gǔ is the hub at the center of a wheel.

glosses.zh: 怎奈向：怎么受得了，无可奈何。“向”是语气词。
glosses.en: zěn nài xiàng: how can one bear it. Xiàng is just a filler word here.

glosses.zh: 兰成：南北朝诗人庾信的小名。他被留在北方回不了南方，写过很多思念故乡的悲伤作品。
glosses.en: lán chéng: the childhood name of Yu Xin, a poet of the Southern and Northern Dynasties. Kept in the north and unable to go home, he wrote many sad works of homesickness.

glosses.zh: 憔悴：又瘦又疲惫的样子。
glosses.en: qiáo cuì: thin and worn out.

glosses.zh: 卫玠：晋朝有名的美男子，身体很弱，常常生病。
glosses.en: wèi jiè: Wei Jie, a famously handsome man of the Jin dynasty who was frail and often ill.

glosses.zh: 清羸：清瘦虚弱。
glosses.en: qīng léi: thin and weak.

glosses.zh: 等闲时：平平常常的时候，随随便便。
glosses.en: děng xián shí: at any ordinary moment.

glosses.zh: 易伤心目：眼里看到的东西很容易让人伤心。
glosses.en: yì shāng xīn mù: what the eyes see easily hurts the heart.

glosses.zh: 平阳客：东汉马融在平阳客居时，听到有人吹笛，非常悲伤，写下了《长笛赋》。这里词人用来比自己。
glosses.en: píng yáng kè: the guest at Pingyang. Ma Rong of the Eastern Han, staying away from home at Pingyang, heard someone play the flute, was deeply moved, and wrote a famous piece about the flute. The poet compares himself to him.

glosses.zh: 况：何况。
glosses.en: kuàng: what's more.

glosses.zh: 萧索：冷落凄凉。
glosses.en: xiāo suǒ: bleak and desolate.

glosses.zh: 青芜国：长满青草的地方。芜，杂草。
glosses.en: qīng wú guó: a land overgrown with green weeds.

glosses.zh: 红糁：红色的碎粒，指被雨打落的花瓣。
glosses.en: hóng sǎn: red bits, meaning petals knocked down by the rain.

glosses.zh: 荆桃：樱桃。
glosses.en: jīng táo: cherries.

glosses.zh: 如菽：像豆子一样小。菽，豆子。
glosses.en: rú shū: as small as beans.

glosses.zh: 秉烛：拿着蜡烛。古诗里说“昼短苦夜长，何不秉烛游”，劝人抓紧时间夜里也去游玩。
glosses.en: bǐng zhú: holding a candle. An old poem said that since days are short and nights long, why not go out at night with a candle in hand.

translation.zh: 对面笼了一夜的烟雾刚刚散去，
translation.en: The mist that hung all night across the way has just cleared.

translation.zh: 春天的鸟儿都安静下来，
translation.en: The spring birds have gone quiet.

translation.zh: 飞来的雨点不时敲响高高的屋顶。
translation.en: Flying rain now and then drums on the high roof.

translation.zh: 墙头一竿竿新竹像青玉色的旗子，
translation.en: Above the wall the new bamboo stands like green-jade banners.

translation.zh: 竹子上的白粉都被雨洗干净了，
translation.en: The rain has washed off all their white powder,

translation.zh: 嫩嫩的竹梢互相碰来碰去。
translation.en: and their tender tips brush against each other.

translation.zh: 潮气逼进了琴弦，
translation.en: The damp seeps into the qin strings.

translation.zh: 寒气侵入了枕边的屏风，
translation.en: The cold creeps into the screen by my pillow.

translation.zh: 蛛网被风吹得粘在竹帘上。
translation.en: Cobwebs blow and stick to the bamboo blind.

translation.zh: 在这没有人的驿站里，
translation.en: In this empty roadside station,

translation.zh: 我听着屋檐滴雨，一声接一声，
translation.en: I listen to the eaves dripping without end,

translation.zh: 困极了，刚刚睡熟。
translation.en: so tired I have just fallen sound asleep.

translation.zh: 可惜忧愁太重，一下子又惊醒了，
translation.en: But my sorrow is so heavy that I wake with a start.

translation.zh: 梦太浅，什么也记不住，
translation.en: The dream was so faint I cannot remember it,

translation.zh: 只能可怜自己孤孤单单。
translation.en: and I can only pity myself, so alone.

translation.zh: 我这个在外的人，想快点回家，
translation.en: I am a traveler, longing to hurry home.

translation.zh: 最担心的是路上的雨水挡住车轮。
translation.en: My first worry is the rainwater on the road that will stop the wheels.

translation.zh: 怎么受得了啊，我像庾信一样憔悴，
translation.en: How can I bear it? I am worn out like Yu Xin,

translation.zh: 像卫玠一样清瘦虚弱，
translation.en: thin and frail like Wei Jie,

translation.zh: 平常随便看到什么，都容易伤心。
translation.en: and anything I see, even on an ordinary day, hurts my heart.

translation.zh: 难怪当年客居平阳的马融，
translation.en: No wonder Ma Rong, the guest at Pingyang,

translation.zh: 听到笛中的哀曲会落下两行泪。
translation.en: shed tears when he heard a sad tune on the flute.

translation.zh: 何况这里冷落凄凉，长满青草，
translation.en: What's more, this place is bleak and overgrown with green weeds.

translation.zh: 被雨打落的红花瓣铺满了地，
translation.en: Red petals knocked down by the rain cover the ground,

translation.zh: 门外的樱桃才像豆子那么小。
translation.en: and outside the gate the cherries are only as small as beans.

translation.zh: 夜里想拿着蜡烛出去游玩，又有谁陪我呢？
translation.en: If I went out at night with a candle, who would come with me?

background.zh: 这首词题为“春雨”，写的是词人在外地赶路时，被春雨困在路边驿站里的情景。具体写作时间和地点都不清楚。周邦彦一生做官，常在各地之间奔波，这首词里那种孤单、想回家的心情，和他长期漂泊在外的经历有关。上段写雨中所见所闻，下段写思归的愁苦。
background.en: This lyric is titled "Spring Rain". It shows the poet on a journey, kept by spring rain at a roadside post station. The exact time and place are not known. As an official, Zhou Bangyan often traveled from post to post, and the loneliness and longing for home here fit that long life on the road. The first part shows what he sees and hears in the rain; the second part shows his sorrow and wish to go home.

author_note.zh: 周邦彦（1056—1121），字美成，号清真居士，北宋词人。他精通音乐，写景特别细腻，常常从很小的地方下笔，比如竹上的白粉、琴弦的潮气、竹帘上的蛛网。他还爱化用古人的故事和诗句，让短短一首词里装进许多层意思。
author_note.en: Zhou Bangyan (1056–1121), courtesy name Meicheng, was a Northern Song lyric poet. He was an expert in music and painted scenes with great care, often starting from tiny things: the powder on bamboo, the damp in the qin strings, a cobweb on a blind. He also loved to borrow old stories and lines, so that a short lyric holds many layers of meaning.

appreciation.zh: 上段几乎一句一个细节，把春雨写得又湿又冷：雨点敲屋顶，新竹被洗得干干净净，琴弦受潮，枕边发凉，连蛛网都被吹得粘在帘子上。词人一直没直接说“雨”有多大，我们却能感到潮气扑面。他在空荡荡的驿站里好不容易睡着，又被愁惊醒，梦也记不住。下段转到心里：想回家，却怕雨水挡路；他把自己比作憔悴的庾信、瘦弱的卫玠、听笛落泪的马融，一层层加深愁苦。最后，满地落花，樱桃还小，春天快过去了，夜里想秉烛出游，却没人陪。一场春雨，写出了旅人全部的孤单。
appreciation.en: In the first part almost every line adds a detail, and the spring rain feels wet and cold. Raindrops drum on the roof. The new bamboo is washed clean. The qin strings are damp, the pillow is chilly, and even the cobwebs are blown onto the blind. The poet never says outright how hard it rains, yet we can feel the damp on our faces. In the empty station he finally falls asleep, only to be woken by sorrow, and he cannot recall the dream. The second part turns inward. He wants to go home but fears the water on the road. He compares himself to the worn-out Yu Xin, the frail Wei Jie, and Ma Rong weeping at a flute tune, each one deepening the sadness. At the end, petals cover the ground, the cherries are still small, and spring is nearly gone. He would go out at night with a candle, but no one would come. One spring rain holds all of a traveler's loneliness.
